title: Symmetry Constraints Regularize Neural Quantum State Learning
authors: Turbasu Chatterjee, Manas Sajjan, Songbo Xie, Elliott Love, Vinit Singh, Bojko N. Bakalov, Sabre Kais
abstract: Neural quantum states (NQS) offer highly expressive variational wavefunctions, but their optimization is frequently bottlenecked by redundant parameters and poorly conditioned landscapes. We demonstrate that embedding Hamiltonian symmetries directly into the variational parameterization geometrically regularizes this learning problem. For Boltzmann-family NQS, we enforce symmetries by tying local Pauli-$Z$ generators along physical geometric orbits, analytically collapsing the trainable coefficient space prior to optimization. To quantify the resulting optimization geometry, we introduce a geometric metric built on the Jacobian and Hessian of the optimization landscape. This framework evaluates the fraction of the physically accessible state space that corresponds to high-quality, low-energy solutions. Evaluating our approach on transverse-field Ising (TFIM) and XXZ spin chains shows that symmetry compilation excises the vast majority of parameters while maintaining ground-state accuracy within the resolution of the reported benchmarks. In large TFIM systems, strong spatial constraints compress thousands of parameters down to tens, delivering substantial runtime accelerations. Our geometric diagnostics indicate that symmetry produces a more favorable target-aware geometry by concentrating the reachable state space around low-energy solutions while retaining broad target basins. Together, our results indicate that symmetry compilation concentrates the expressive power of NQS on states relevant to the target problem, thereby reducing model size and training cost without sacrificing accuracy.
summary: This paper shows that incorporating known Hamiltonian symmetries directly into Neural Quantum State parameterizations acts as a powerful geometric regularizer. By structurally collapsing redundant parameters using techniques like null-space projection, it drastically reduces model size and training time for systems like TFIM chains. This method concentrates the NQS expressive power onto physically relevant low-energy states.
main_problem: Neural Quantum States (NQS) suffer from optimization bottlenecks due to redundant parameters and poorly conditioned energy landscapes.
main_result: Embedding Hamiltonian symmetries directly into the parameterization structurally collapses the trainable parameter space, significantly reducing model size and training cost without sacrificing ground-state accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a geometric metric based on the Jacobian and Hessian of the optimization landscape to quantify how symmetry constraints regularize the search space by eliminating redundant degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The work analyzes NQS parameterized for many-body wavefunctions, tested specifically on the Transverse-Field Ising (TFIM) and XXZ spin chains using a Boltzmann-family ansatz.
key_observables: Geometric metrics including the Jacobian/Hessian analysis, active Fubini–Study dimension, local good volume fraction ($	ext{fg}_{	ext{good}}$), and parameter count reduction.
important_parameters: System size (N), Hamiltonian parameters ($J=h=1$), and various symmetry constraints (e.g., translations, reflections, bitflip parity).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that structural constraint imposition via null-space projection accurately captures the physically relevant subspace of the variational manifold.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how symmetry reduction quotients redundant directions in parameter space while preserving the volume of accurate solutions; consistency checks confirm this compression across multiple geometric proxies.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of NQS optimization bottlenecks, then details the method of embedding symmetries by constraining parameters via global constraint matrices. It rigorously analyzes the geometry using various rank and volume estimators before concluding that symmetry compilation is a robust regularization technique.
why_interesting: For AMO physicists working with complex Hamiltonians (like those describing trapped ions or molecular interactions), this provides a systematic, mathematically rigorous way to reduce the dimensionality of variational ansatzes derived from symmetries inherent in the physical Hamiltonian.
